types.name: TableColumn
types.doc: Table's per-column shape: stable string id (echoed in sortChanged), header title, optional fixed width in px.

types.name: TableRow
types.doc: Table's per-row shape: cells are positional, indexed by the columns array order.

types.name: TreeNode
types.doc: TreeView's flat node shape, keyed by id/parentId (root nodes omit parentId). Leaf-row fields (title/badge/iconName) match SourceList's row shape so cell rendering can be shared.

types.name: SourceTreeAction
types.doc: One trailing row affordance, declared once in the widget's `actions` prop and referenced by nodes via actionIds.

types.name: SourceTreeNode
types.doc: Flat id/parentId sidebar row (root rows omit parentId). `section` marks a non-selectable group header; expansion is app-controlled state, never native state. `iconName` is a freedesktop icon name; `iconData` is raw image bytes as a data URL or bare base64 (what faviconChanged hands you) and WINS over iconName when both are set.

types.name: CommandPaletteItem
types.doc: CommandPalette result row: stable string id (echoed in onActivate), title, optional subtitle + leading icon. The app supplies rows already filtered and ordered; the widget renders them in order and never filters or reorders.

types.name: ChartPoint
types.doc: One datum. `x`/`y` are the numeric axes; `label` names the point on a category axis and names the slice on a pie. The OHLC quartet carries candlestick bodies and wicks and is ignored by every other chart type (which read `y`).

types.name: ChartSeries
types.doc: One plotted series: stable id (echoed in pointSelected), legend label, optional explicit `#rrggbb` colour (omitted takes the next slot of the platform's accent-seeded ramp), and its points in draw order. The widget never sorts, filters or mutates points — the app owns the data, as with Table's rows.

types.name: CodeDiagnostic
types.doc: One squiggle in a CodeEditor: 1-based line, 1-based column, severity ("error" | "warning" | "info" | "hint"), and the message shown on hover. The widget renders what it is handed and never analyses the text itself — a language server lives in app-side TS, the same division Table draws between its rows and their source.

widgets.name: Overlay
widgets.doc: Z-stack container: the first child is the content and fills the overlay; every later child floats above it, positioned by its own halign/valign/margin style keys. The layer a floating load bar or badge needs without taking layout space from the content.
